question.text: For valuation of debt investments (including mezzanine capital and preference shares with predictable cash flows) held by a Cat II debt AIF, IPEV 2022 recommends:

answer.text: Simple coupon-accrual method regardless of market yield
Listed equity P/E of the issuer
DCF of the future cash flows at an appropriate market-based discount rate

explanation.text: The Logic: Per PDF Section 11.8.3 point 6: 'DCF of the future cash flows would be a good way of valuing such entities or debt instruments. The same approach may be used for sub-ordinate debt, mezzanine capital and preference share investments which have predictable cash flows.' For distressed/non-performing debt, the discount rate reflects the market purchaser's required yield. The Trap: Historical cost ignores credit spread movement; coupon-accrual without MTM distorts NAV; P/E is irrelevant for debt. DCF with market yield is the IPEV norm for debt. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C covers same. Series-VII (Securities Ops) tests bond accounting with YTM-based accrual. Ind-AS 109 financial instruments categorisation (HTM, FVTOCI, FVTPL) is tested in CA Final. Manager's Pro-Tip: For Cat II debt AIFs, build a market-yield curve from comparable-rated listed corporate bonds refreshed quarterly. Valuer should apply this curve to your unlisted NCDs. Document the curve methodology in the Valuation Policy — auditors always probe this.
